location: iast/crypto/hash/orchestrion.yml (prepend __dd__iast_ReportWeakHash__ via go:linkname); iast/crypto/cipher/orchestrion.yml; internal/vulnerability/report.go:37-52; internal/spans/vulnerability.go:18; internal/spans/annotation.go:29-31,52
title: Weak-crypto hooks panic during package init: IAST runs before spans/tracer are initialized
claim: The linkname-injected crypto hooks bypass Go init ordering. After internal/config initializes (Enabled defaults to true) but before dd-trace-go tracer and internal/spans initialize, any md5/sha1/des/rc4 use in a package init calls vulnerability.Report, and it panics (nil global tracer type assertion in tracer.StartSpan, or nil spans globals). Nothing recovers, so the process crashes before main.
repro_command: cd <copy>/_repro/initorder && GOFLAGS='-p=4 -mod=mod' GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go tool orchestrion go build -o initorder . && ./initorder

title: Only three bridges have a panic boundary; the other hook entry points run unshielded in host goroutines
claim: HTTP, reader, URL, writer, operator, scope-finish, span-finish and crypto hooks call IAST code without recover. No reachable panic was found today, but host safety depends only on per-site proofs.

title: A recovered sink panic would leak store locks that are unlocked manually rather than deferred
claim: Sink bridges recover, but the store and request code they call unlocks TryLock/TryRLock manually. A panic in those regions would leave locks held (permanent drops, or a deadlock on Finish). Latent: the critical sections are currently panic-free.
